concepts.title: Angles, Radian Measure and Degree Conversion
concepts.definition: An angle is formed by rotating a ray from an initial position, measured in degrees where one full rotation is 360 degrees or in radians where one full rotation is two pi, and the relation pi radians equals 180 degrees converts between the measures.
concepts.textbook_ref: Radian measure makes arc length equal to radius times the angle, which simplifies formulas of trigonometry and calculus.

concepts.title: Trigonometric Functions, Identities and Their Signs
concepts.definition: Trigonometric functions of sine, cosine, tangent, cosecant, secant and cotangent are defined on the unit circle, with signs decided by the quadrant through the ASTC rule, fundamental identities like sin squared plus cos squared equal to one, and periodicity of two pi for sine cosine and secant cosecant and pi for tangent cotangent.
concepts.key_idea: Identities such as sin squared x plus cos squared x equals one, and complementary angle relations like sin of ninety minus x equal cos x, run through all trigonometric work.

concepts.title: Compound Angles, Sum-Difference Formulas and General Solutions
concepts.definition: Trigonometry develops sum and difference formulas like sin of A plus B, double angle formulas, and solutions of trigonometric equations given as general solutions such as x equals n pi plus alpha for equations of the sine type, with the principal solution in the first circle.
concepts.key_idea: The sum and difference formulas convert compound angles into products, and general solutions list every angle satisfying a trigonometric equation.
